{{< include /_macros.qmd >}}

A *Kakeya set* in $\F_q^n$ is a set $K$ that contains a line in every direction: for every $v \in \F_q^n \setminus \set{0}$ there is a point $x$ with $\set{x + tv : t \in \F_q} \subseteq K$. Wolff asked whether every such set has size at least $c_n q^n$,[^wolff] and Dvir answered the question with a remarkably short argument.

[^wolff]: Wolff raised the question in 1999 as a finite field model of the Euclidean Kakeya conjecture.

## Two facts about polynomials

::: {#lem-interpolation}
## Interpolation
If $E \subseteq \F^n$ is finite and $\abs{E} < \binom{d+n}{n}$, then some nonzero polynomial $P \in \F[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ of degree at most $d$ vanishes on $E$.
:::

::: {.proof}
The polynomials of degree at most $d$ form a vector space of dimension

$$
\dim \F[x_1, \dots, x_n]_{\le d} = \binom{d+n}{n},
$$ {#eq-dimension}

since the right side counts monomials of degree at most $d$. Evaluation at the points of $E$ is a linear map from this space to $\F^E$. By @eq-dimension the domain has larger dimension than the codomain, so the kernel is nontrivial.
:::

::: {#lem-nonvanishing}
If $Q \in \F_q[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ is nonzero and has degree less than $q$ in each variable, then $Q$ does not vanish on all of $\F_q^n$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Induct on $n$. For $n = 1$, a nonzero polynomial of degree less than $q$ has fewer than $q$ roots. For $n > 1$, write $Q = \sum_{i < q} Q_i(x_1, \dots, x_{n-1})\, x_n^i$ with some $Q_i \ne 0$. By induction there is $a \in \F_q^{n-1}$ with $Q_i(a) \ne 0$, so $Q(a, x_n)$ is a nonzero polynomial in $x_n$ of degree less than $q$, and it has a non-root.
:::

## The theorem

::: {#thm-dvir}
## Dvir, 2009
Every Kakeya set $K \subseteq \F_q^n$ satisfies
$$
\abs{K} \ge \binom{q+n-1}{n} \ge \frac{q^n}{n!}.
$$
:::

::: {.proof}
Suppose $\abs{K} < \binom{q+n-1}{n}$. Applying @lem-interpolation with $d = q - 1$ gives a nonzero polynomial $P$ of degree at most $q - 1$ that vanishes on $K$. Let $d = \deg P$ and let $P_d$ be the homogeneous part of $P$ of degree $d$. Since $K$ is nonempty, $P$ is not a nonzero constant, so $d \ge 1$.

Fix a direction $v \ne 0$ and choose $x$ with $x + tv \in K$ for all $t \in \F_q$. The polynomial $g(t) = P(x + tv)$ has degree at most $d \le q - 1$ and vanishes at all $q$ elements of $\F_q$, so $g \equiv 0$. Its coefficient of $t^d$ is $P_d(v)$, hence $P_d(v) = 0$. Since $P_d$ is homogeneous of degree $d \ge 1$, also $P_d(0) = 0$.

So $P_d$ vanishes on all of $\F_q^n$, yet it is nonzero with degree less than $q$ in each variable. This contradicts @lem-nonvanishing.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Remark
Using polynomials that vanish to high multiplicity, Dvir, Kopparty, Saraf, and Sudan improved the constant in @thm-dvir from $1/n!$ to $2^{-n}$.
:::
